title: Apple crumble with oats and hazelnuts

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Apples, flour, butter, oats, demerara, hazelnuts, yoghurt, lemon and cinnamon are all plain home-kitchen staples.

supermarket.reason: Every item, including the hazelnuts, is an everyday supermarket buy at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a baking dish, a bowl and an oven, and rubbing in is a beginner technique.

works.reason: Six apples under a 75g flour and 75g oat topping, baked at 190°C for 30 to 35 minutes, gives a sensible crumble for four, and eating apples are sweet enough without extra sugar.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes is realistic for coring six apples, rubbing in and chopping nuts, and the 35-minute cook matches the bake.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears in the steps.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm apple crumble suits mid-January, and the stored apples are clearly the point of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English that a neighbour could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is fruit-heavy, with oats, nuts and yoghurt and a modest 40g of sugar for four, so it makes a wholesome treat a family would make again.
